description:
Project: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling).

Goal
- Reduce user-visible p95 tail latency for text generation under mixed prompt-length distributions (short chat prompts interleaved with long-context prompts) without materially regressing throughput or fairness.

Problem framing
- Redwood’s continuous batching and KV-cache-heavy decode path performs well in steady-state homogeneous workloads, but mixed workloads can cause head-of-line blocking where long-prefill or long-context requests dominate GPU scheduling and queue selection, inflating p95.
- The prototype introduces a short/long prompt-aware policy (two-queue or class-based scheduling) to bias service toward latency-sensitive short prompts while still guaranteeing progress for long prompts.

Scope
- Runtime scheduler changes: request classification, queueing, dispatch policy, and guardrails (aging, starvation prevention, max skew, burst caps).
- Kernel/runtime interactions: prefill vs decode separation, token budgeting, and ensuring kernel selection doesn’t thrash when mixing sequence lengths.
- Observability: new scheduler metrics/traces (queue depth by class, time-in-queue, prefill latency, per-class p50/p95, starvation counters).
- Benchmarking and evaluation: synthetic mixes (e.g., 80/20 short/long), replay of anonymized production traces, and perf-canary integration.
- Rollout: feature flag + config knobs; staged canary in one region and a subset of Dedicated pools; rollback plan.

Out of scope (for prototype phase)
- Full multi-tenant QoS productization (customer-configurable classes/tiers beyond internal knobs).
- Large-scale admission control redesign (only minimal coupling to existing backpressure).

Stakeholders and roles
- Eng Serving Runtime (Scheduling): Sofia Ivanova (EM), Lena Fischer (tech lead), Marcus Reed, Omar El‑Sayed, Julian Moore.
- Eng Serving Runtime (Kernels): Hiro Tanaka (EM), Grace Kim, Yuki Sato.
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant, Rafael Mendes, Aisha Bello.
- Product alignment: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated), Paula Mendes (rollout telemetry requirements).

Timeline and milestones (hypothetical)
- Phase 0 (1–2 wks): workload analysis + design review + ADR.
- Phase 1 (2–4 wks): implement scheduler prototype behind flag + instrumentation + unit/regression tests.
- Phase 2 (2–3 wks): benchmark suite + perf-canary + iterate on policy parameters.
- Phase 3 (1–2 wks): limited production canary + SLO monitoring + decision to graduate/iterate.

Key deliverables
- Confluence design + ADRs; benchmark methodology + results; runbook/rollout plan.
- Linear initiative with tracked tasks and dependencies.
- GitHub PR series implementing the prototype and follow-up fixes.
- Slack coordination threads across runtime, SRE, and releases.
- (Optional) customer-facing escalations captured via Jira + sales/CS artifacts when the work is triggered by real customer pain.
